causes.text: Intel announced that its 7 nanometer chip manufacturing technology was six months behind schedule, forcing it to consider outsourcing more production and signalling that rivals like TSMC were pulling ahead.

source_info.title: Intel chip delay forces shift to using more outside factories, shares drop

effects.text: Apple became the first publicly listed U.S. company valued at more than $2 trillion as its shares briefly climbed to $468.65 and finished the day up around 1.2%, reflecting investor confidence in its shift toward services and device sales.

source_info.title: Apple becomes first U.S. company to reach a $2 trillion market cap

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2020-07-23, Intel 7nm delay signaled technological lag, shifting investor confidence to firms with stronger manufacturing execution like TSMC.
Since Apple depends on TSMC for its chip production, Apple was perceived as relatively shielded and competitively advantaged.
Investors interpreted Apple supplier resilience as a signal of reliable performance, increasing stock buying interest.
On 2020-08-19, Apple stock rose by 1.2% on August 19, 2020, lifting its valuation above $2 trillion.

rationale: Intel delay reaffirmed TSMC's edge. As Apple relies on TSMC, the market saw Apple as a safer, forward-looking tech investment, driving up its share price.
counterfactual_analysis: If Intel had delivered 7nm chips on time, TSMC would not have gained such a clear edge, and Apple shares might not have surged to record highs so soon.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Also boosted confidence in its long-term prospects
Created a favorable macro backdrop for Apple

details.commentary: Intel's delay on 7nm chips widened the technology gap with TSMC, strengthening TSMC's position as the leading advanced foundry. For Apple, being tied to a stronger manufacturing partner reduced competitive risk in high-end devices and reinforced investor confidence in its long-term product roadmap.
